How native advertising broke the review site

A sponsored post used to be obvious. It sat in a box, it carried a label, and a reader could skip it without reading a word. The modern version is a paragraph in the middle of an otherwise honest article, written in the same voice as everything around it.

Disclosure rules exist and are mostly followed in letter. A line reading paid partnership at the top of a page satisfies the regulator, and nothing about it survives into the excerpt an aggregator shows.

The word advertising has quietly stopped meaning a banner. In a 2023 survey of review sites, most of the commercial content that readers failed to identify carried a correct disclosure somewhere on the page.

What changed is who reads the page. An agent summarising ten reviews carries the recommendation forward and drops the label, because the label is markup and the recommendation is prose.

Regulators are still writing rules for a reader who scrolls. The reader that matters now does not scroll, and it does not see boxes at all.
